sub_scenario.family: prepared public representation versus live improvised exposure
sub_scenario.one_line: science museum educator: evening series first on the record

dialogue.content: I spent the first hour tidying the show script and closing stale entries.
Anything still open?
Two items, both with owners.
The exhibit notes review wrapped early today.
Any surprises in it?
None worth recording.
Impromptu chats at exhibit stations are pleasant and low-stakes.
Casual improvisation is fine.
Casual is the keyword.
Someone new shadowed me in the planetarium dome this morning.
Did that slow you down?
A little, but the questions were good ones.
I batched my replies about the visitor sessions into one message before lunch.
Cleaner than drip-feeding answers.
Much cleaner.
My scripted planetarium evening shows, rehearsed twice before opening, hold the museum's top visitor scores three seasons running.
The rehearsed format owns the scoreboard.
Three seasons of it.
Question segments after a scripted show go well; the script gives me the floor to improvise from.
Bounded improvisation on a prepared base.
The base is what makes it bounded.
I archived last cycle's notes on the exhibit notes and set up the new folder.
A fresh start?
As fresh as these things get.
The education director renewed the evening series specifically on those scores.
The record has institutional consequences.
Renewal-shaped consequences.
A vendor call about the show script ran long but ended well.
Worth the time?
This one, yes.
I walked through the planetarium dome checklist with the new starter.
How did they do?
Careful and quick, a good sign.
Quiet afternoon; I cleared the backlog around the visitor sessions.
A rare day.
I did not waste it.
I flagged a small inconsistency in the exhibit notes records and fixed it at the source.
Root cause or symptom?
Root cause, for once.
The unscripted ask-me-anything floor cart, when I trialed it for a month, produced my two lowest-rated sessions ever and one factual correction posted publicly on the board.
The unscripted format produced the record's floor.
The floor and the correction, both.
I sketched next week's plan for the visitor sessions before leaving.
Ahead of schedule?
Ahead enough to sleep well.
Lunch walk, then a clean pass through the show script updates.
Does the walk help?
It resets the afternoon.
Both open roles carry the same hours and stipend this season.
Externals cancel again.
Conveniently, yes.
A colleague says the cart is where educators show real command of their material.
Command theater.
Theater with a public corrections board.
I closed the week by updating the planetarium dome handover notes.
Anything unusual to hand over?
Blessedly little.
Season assignments are due: the scripted evening show series or the ask-me-anything floor cart first on my form?
